title: I'm turning 35: 28 hard-won startup rules from John Rush
summary: John Rush lists 28 lessons from a decade of failed and successful startups. Core themes: validate before building, chase users not investors, bootstrap, charge more, go paid-only, skip corporates and outsourcing, do SEO and daily posting early, and build for audiences you love.

principles.text: Sell features before building them: chat daily with users about ideas and only build what resonates.
principles.quote: I run DMs with 10-20 users every day, where I chat about all my ideas and features I wanna add. I clearly see what resonates with me most and only go build those.

principles.text: Chase users, not investors; investor interest follows traction.
principles.quote: Chase users, and then investors will be chasing you.

principles.text: No free tier until the product is validated; free users push you to build a perfect free product.
principles.quote: Free and paid users often need different products. Don't fall into this trap as I did.

principles.text: Don't price lowest. $50 customers are happier and better advocates than $5 customers.
principles.quote: The audience on $5 and $50 are totally different.

principles.text: Landing page is minor early; first sales happen outside the website.
principles.quote: Your first 100 sales happen outside of the website.

principles.text: Start SEO as early as possible; ignoring it was his biggest regret.
principles.quote: I ignored this for 14 years, and it's my biggest regret.
